subject: Follow-up: Buying process checklist & next steps for Redwood inference pilot
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Malik <dana.malik@finservco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Buying process checklist & next steps for Redwood inference pilot

Hi Dana — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + what I need from your side to keep momentum: 

Summary of outcome
- Agreed pilot: 3-month evaluation of Redwood inference for customer-facing model endpoints (~2k qps peak simulated).
- Success criteria: <10% latency tail, per-token cost target, and integration with your internal auth/proxy.

Procurement & commercial checklist (please confirm):
1) Billing method: PO (net30) or company card? Which is preferred?
2) Vendor onboarding: do you require a completed vendor form / W9 / insurance? If so, please share the onboarding contact or the form.
3) Marketplace option: if you prefer to avoid vendor onboarding, can the team buy through AWS Marketplace (we can publish a marketplace offer)?
4) Legal: do you need an SOW + MSA redline? Who is the legal reviewer?
5) Budget owner & approver: who signs the PO / signs contract?
6) Timing: desired start date for pilot / any blackout dates for procurement.

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft SOW and our pricing grid to make internal approvals easier.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm items 1–5 above or point me to the procurement contact.
- If PO route: please send vendor onboarding form and expected PO lead time.
- If marketplace: we’ll prepare a marketplace listing and share procurement guidance to speed purchase.

Happy to join a short call with procurement if helpful. Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF)]
[attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Grid.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Dana Malik <dana.malik@finservco.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finservco.com>, Evan Li <evan.li@finservco.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-13T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Buying process checklist & next steps for Redwood inference pilot

Hi Sergio — thanks for the clear recap. Short answers below and looping procurement.

1) Billing method: Our default is PO (Net30). We can do a credit card for small pilots but finance prefers PO for vendor tracking.
2) Vendor onboarding: Yes — attached is our vendor form. Procurement needs a completed vendor form, W9, and certificate of insurance for agreements over $25k.
3) Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is an option but requires our procurement to validate the offer SKU and pricing model. It could be faster but not guaranteed.
4) Legal: We will need an SOW and a redline to your MSA. Legal reviewer is Evan Li (cc’d).
5) Budget owner: Evan Li is the approver. He will confirm budget availability this week.
6) Timing: If onboarding paperwork starts this week, procurement estimates 2–3 weeks to issue the PO.

I’ve attached the vendor form here. @procurement@finservco.com — can you confirm the portal link and any additional documents you need?

Thanks,
Dana Malik
Director, Platform Partnerships
FinServ Co
[attachment: FinServ_vendor_form.pdf (PDF)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Malik <dana.malik@finservco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@finservco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Buying process checklist & next steps for Redwood inference pilot

Thanks Dana — really helpful. Quick replies and next steps from our side: 

- We can accept PO (Net30) or card. If PO is preferred, please send the completed vendor form back to me and procurement — I’ve attached our W9 and a sample MSA + SOW to accelerate review.
- Marketplace: we do have a Marketplace listing option. If procurement confirms it would be faster, we’ll prioritize a marketplace SKU and share a procurement guide (pricing parity note included).
- Insurance: we can provide COI; will confirm policy limits with our security team and share by EOD tomorrow.
- SOW: attached draft SOW — open to edits. Proposed pilot start: target May 4th so procurement timelines align.

Action items:
- Sergio: supply W9 + MSA + draft SOW (attached).
- Dana / Procurement: confirm preferred purchase path (PO vs marketplace) and estimated PO date.
- Evan: please confirm budget approver and any legal must-haves we should address pre-redline.

If helpful I can set up a 20-minute sync with procurement this week to walk through the vendor form and highlight where we can turn on the pilot quickly.

Regards,
Sergio
[attachment: Redwood_MSA_Sample.pdf (PDF)]
[attachment: Redwood_W9.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@finservco.com>, Dana Malik <dana.malik@finservco.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Buying process checklist & next steps for Redwood inference pilot

Hi all — Ben from Sales Ops at Redwood. Quick note to confirm two billing paths and what we need from procurement to issue invoices: 

Option A — PO (preferred by FinServ):
- We will accept an official PO referencing deal ID FS-7843.
- Send vendor form + PO number; finance will invoice on receipt and follow net30 terms.

Option B — AWS Marketplace:
- If procurement confirms marketplace SKU and purchase flow, we can enable the listing and provide procurement guidance that often shortens approval time. Pricing may differ slightly due to marketplace fees.

If you think PO will take >3 weeks and you want to run the pilot sooner, marketplace is usually the faster route. Happy to join a short call to walk through either path.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
